heading: Licensing & Codes
question: What does a learner's licence test cover?
body: A learner's licence test covers: (i) rules of the road and related legislation, (ii) road traffic signs/signals/markings, and (iii) vehicle controls. Once passed, the learner's licence is valid for 24 months.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: Under what circumstances is a person disqualified from obtaining or holding a licence?
body: A person is disqualified from obtaining or holding a licence: (i) while addicted to narcotics or excessive alcohol use, (ii) while disqualified or suspended by a court or authority, or (iii) during a period following cancellation of a previous licence.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: When is a person prohibited from applying for a licence?
body: A person may not apply for a licence for a class of vehicle they are already licensed to drive under an existing licence.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: Which medical conditions or physical defects disqualify a person from holding a licence?
body: A person is disqualified if suffering from: (i) uncontrolled epilepsy, (ii) disabling giddiness or fainting (e.g. from hypertension), (iii) a mental illness requiring detention or treatment, (iv) a condition causing muscular incoordination, (v) uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, (vi) defective vision below the prescribed standard, or (vii) any other disease or defect likely to prevent safe driving. Deafness alone is not disqualifying.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: What are the restrictions and requirements for holding a Code 1 learner's licence?
body: A Code 1 learner's licence authorises riding a motorcycle (but not a motor quadrucycle) on a public road. (i) Minimum age is 16; (ii) under 18 you're limited to a 125cc engine; (iii) no passengers may be carried.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: What are the conditions, age limit, and validity period for a Code 2 learner's licence?
body: A Code 2 learner's licence authorises driving any motor vehicle or combination (other than a motorcycle or tricycle) with tare, GVM, or GCM not exceeding 3500kg, only under the direct supervision of a licensed driver for that class. (i) Minimum age is 17; (ii) valid for 24 months from the test date.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: What are the conditions, age limit, and validity period for a Code 3 learner's licence?
body: A Code 3 learner's licence authorises driving any motor vehicle or combination (other than a motorcycle, tricycle, or quadrucycle) -- covering both light and heavy vehicles -- only under the direct supervision of a licensed driver for that class. (i) Minimum age is 18; (ii) valid for 24 months from the test date.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are the general condition requirements for a motorcycle's lamps?
body: A motorcycle's lamps must be: (i) undamaged, (ii) properly secured, and (iii) capable of being lit at all times.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When must a motorcycle's headlamp be lit on a public road?
body: A motorcycle's headlamp must be lit at all times when riding on a public road, day and night.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What condition must all lamps on a light or heavy motor vehicle be in?
body: On a light or heavy motor vehicle, all lamps must be: (i) undamaged, (ii) unobscured, (iii) properly secured, and (iv) capable of being lit at all times.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When must headlamps, rear lamps, and number-plate lamps be lit on a motor vehicle?
body: Headlamps, rear lamps, and number-plate lamps must be lit: (i) between sunset and sunrise, and (ii) at any other time when persons and vehicles aren't clearly visible at 150 metres.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When do motor vehicle lighting requirements not apply to a parked vehicle?
body: These lighting rules don't apply to a vehicle parked: (i) off the roadway, (ii) in a demarcated parking place, or (iii) within 12 metres of a lit street lamp illuminating the road.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How far must a headlamp on main beam adequately illuminate the road ahead?
body: Every headlamp on main beam must adequately illuminate the road ahead, enabling the driver to see a person, vehicle, or substantial object at least 100 metres away.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When must a driver dip the main beam of their headlamps?
body: Dip your main beam for: (i) oncoming traffic, and (ii) when following another vehicle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How far must a headlamp on dipped beam adequately illuminate the road ahead?
body: Every headlamp on dipped beam must adequately illuminate the road ahead, enabling the driver to see a person, vehicle, or substantial object at least 45 metres away.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a vehicle be driven using only its parking lamps?
body: A vehicle may not be driven in motion using only its parking lamps.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What rear lamp requirement applies to a motorcycle or motor tricycle?
body: A motorcycle or motor tricycle must be fitted with a rear lamp emitting red light.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What rear lamps are required on a light motor vehicle?
body: A light motor vehicle must be fitted with rear lamps emitting red light.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What rear lamps are required on a heavy motor vehicle?
body: A heavy motor vehicle must be fitted with at least one rear lamp on each side emitting red light.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What stop lamp requirements apply to a light motor vehicle or motorcycle?
body: A light motor vehicle or motorcycle must have rear stop lamps that emit a red light brighter than the rear lamps, visible at 30 metres in normal sunlight.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What stop lamp requirements apply to a heavy motor vehicle?
body: A heavy motor vehicle must have at least one stop lamp on each side at the rear, meeting the same brightness and visibility requirements.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What does an illuminated stop lamp indicate to other road users?
body: An illuminated stop lamp indicates the vehicle is decreasing speed and may stop.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is the requirement for a vehicle's rear number-plate lamp?
body: A vehicle must have at least one number-plate lamp at the rear, making every letter and figure on the plate visible from 20 metres by a person of normal eyesight.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What mounting and approval requirements apply to number plates?
body: A number plate must be: (i) SABS-approved and (ii) fitted so it cannot easily be detached.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What positioning and visibility requirements apply to a number plate?
body: A number plate must be: (i) upright (or within 30 degrees), (ii) with every letter and figure clearly legible and (iii) the whole plate visible.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Which motor vehicles require both front and rear number plates?
body: Motorcycles, motor tricycles, and trailers need only a rear number plate; all other motor vehicles need one at the front and one at the rear.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Under what conditions may fog lamps be used?
body: Fog lamps may only be lit in conditions of poor visibility caused by: (i) snow, (ii) fog, (iii) mist, (iv) dust, or (v) smoke.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Who is permitted to use an adjustable spot lamp on a public road?
body: A vehicle may not use an adjustable spot lamp on a public road, except: (i) official vehicles (ambulance, fire-fighting, police, traffic control), (ii) vehicles used by a medical practitioner or veterinarian for professional duties, or (iii) a breakdown vehicle or utility vehicle working at an accident, breakdown, or overhead line inspection.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What view of the road must a driver have while operating a vehicle?
body: A driver must have a full, clear view of the road ahead, and to the left and right, while the vehicle is in use.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What general rear-view mirror requirement applies to motor vehicles?
body: A vehicle must be fitted with a rear-view mirror giving a clear view of traffic behind in clear weather (tractors are excepted).

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What mirror configuration is required for a motor car, minibus, bus, or goods vehicle?
body: A motor car, minibus, bus, or goods vehicle must have: (i) both an exterior mirror on the driving side and an interior mirror -- or (ii) two exterior mirrors if the interior one doesn't give a clear rear view.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What maintenance and dimension requirements apply to a motorcycle's steering gear?
body: A motorcycle's steering gear must be maintained so it can be steered safely and efficiently, and handlebar width and handgrip height must meet prescribed measurements based on engine capacity.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What maintenance standard is required for a light or heavy motor vehicle's steering gear?
body: A light or heavy motor vehicle's steering gear must be maintained in a condition that allows the vehicle to be steered safely and efficiently.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is the maximum allowed turning radius for a vehicle?
body: A vehicle's turning radius may not exceed 13.1 metres.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What braking systems are required on a motorcycle?
body: A motorcycle must have two independent, working braking systems -- one acting on the front wheel, one on the rear wheel(s).

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What braking systems are required on a light or heavy motor vehicle?
body: A light or heavy motor vehicle must be equipped with a working: (i) service brake, (ii) parking brake, and (iii) emergency brake (the emergency and parking brake may be one and the same).

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When may a driver use a vehicle's hooter?
body: A hooter may only be used when necessary on the grounds of safety.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What functional requirement applies to a light motor vehicle's hooter?
body: A light motor vehicle must have a working hooter, audible by a person of normal hearing from 90 metres.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a private vehicle be fitted with a tune-playing siren or horn?
body: A tune-playing siren or horn may not be used on a private vehicle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must a driver respond when an emergency vehicle sounds a siren and displays warning lights?
body: A driver must immediately give way to any emergency vehicle sounding a siren and displaying warning lights.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Which vehicles are classified as emergency vehicles?
body: Emergency vehicles include: (i) fire-fighting, rescue, and emergency medical/ambulance vehicles (red light), (ii) a vehicle driven by a traffic officer on duty (blue light), and (iii) a vehicle engaged in civil protection (green light).

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: For whom is wearing a seatbelt compulsory while a vehicle moves forward?
body: Seatbelts are compulsory for children and adults aged 3 and older while the vehicle is moving forward.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When must rear-seat passengers wear seatbelts?
body: If seatbelts are fitted, rear-seat passengers must wear them while the vehicle is being driven.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How is a child defined for seatbelt compliance purposes?
body: A child is defined as aged 3 to 14, unless taller than 1.5 metres, in which case they're treated as an adult regardless of age.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When is an adult prohibited from sitting in a seat without wearing a seatbelt?
body: An adult may not occupy a seat without wearing a seatbelt, nor a seat on a row without seatbelts if a belted seat on that row is available.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What seating and restraint duties does a driver owe to a child passenger?
body: A driver must ensure a child uses an appropriate child restraint where available, or a seatbelt if no restraint is available; if no belted seat is available and the vehicle has a rear seat, the child must sit there.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When is wearing a seatbelt not compulsory?
body: It is not compulsory to wear a seatbelt while reversing or moving in or out of a parking bay or area.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What helmet requirements apply to motorcycle, tricycle, and quadrucycle riders and passengers?
body: A motorcycle, tricycle, or quadrucycle rider and any passenger (including a sidecar passenger) must wear a properly fitted, purpose-designed protective helmet with the chin strap fastened.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What duty does a motorcycle rider have regarding passengers under 14 years old?
body: A rider must ensure any passenger under 14 years old also wears a protective helmet.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When are protective helmets not required for motorcycle riders and passengers?
body: Helmets aren't required if the motorcycle has SABS-compliant seatbelts and the engine cannot run unless the rider and any passenger are wearing them.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What visibility and material requirements apply to a light motor vehicle's windscreen?
body: A light motor vehicle's windscreen must give the driver sufficient visibility for safe driving, be made of safety glass, and allow at least 70% light transmittance.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What requirement applies to windscreen wipers on a vehicle fitted with a windscreen?
body: A light or heavy motor vehicle with a windscreen must have at least one wiper that continuously, evenly, and adequately clears the area directly in front of the driver.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What standard must a vehicle's exhaust silencer meet?
body: A vehicle must have an efficient exhaust silencer that channels exhaust gas through it.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What restriction applies to exhaust smoke density from a vehicle?
body: Exhaust smoke may not be dense enough to be a nuisance, or to obstruct other road users' vision.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Where may a vehicle's exhaust not be positioned or leak gas?
body: The exhaust may not be positioned where oil or flammable liquid could drip onto it, and may not leak gas or smoke into the cab or passenger compartment.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Fuel Tank, Electrical Wiring and Battery
question: When is a vehicle prohibited from being used due to fuel system or electrical defects?
body: A vehicle may not be used if its fuel tank, carburettor, or fuel pipes are defective or exposed as a danger, if the fuel tank lacks an effective cap, or if the electrical wiring and battery aren't properly installed, insulated, and maintained.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must a motor vehicle's engine be covered?
body: A light or heavy motor vehicle's engine must be covered so that it isn't a source of danger.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Which vehicles are required to carry an emergency warning triangle?
body: Heavy motor vehicles, goods vehicles, minibuses, and buses (but not motor cars, ambulances, or motorcycles) must carry at least one emergency warning triangle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Where may warning triangles for a combination of vehicles be carried?
body: For a combination of vehicles, the warning triangle for each vehicle in the combination may all be carried on the drawing vehicle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How and where must a warning triangle be placed for a stationary vehicle?
body: A stationary vehicle must place a warning triangle: (i) at least 45 metres away in the direction traffic will approach from, (ii) at roughly the same distance from the roadway edge as the vehicle's own centre, (iii) with the reflective side facing oncoming traffic.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When is a stationary vehicle exempt from placing a warning triangle?
body: A warning triangle isn't required if the vehicle is stopped: (i) in a loading zone, (ii) on a traffic officer's or sign's direction, (iii) because of other traffic while the driver stays in the driving seat, or (iv) during a state or municipal function.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What restriction applies to operating a vehicle that causes excessive noise?
body: A vehicle may not be operated on a public road in a manner that causes excessive noise.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Which vehicles are required to be equipped with a working speedometer?
body: A vehicle capable of reaching 60 km/h or more must be equipped with a working speedometer.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What general speed limits apply on public roads when no sign is displayed?
body: A general speed limit applies to all roads even without a sign: (i) 60 km/h in urban areas, (ii) 100 km/h on non-freeway roads outside urban areas, and (iii) 120 km/h on freeways, unless a sign indicates otherwise.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is the legal consequence of exceeding the applicable speed limit?
body: Exceeding the applicable speed limit is an offence.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Speed Limit for Passenger Vehicles Conveying Persons for Reward
question: What speed limit applies to passenger vehicles conveying persons for reward?
body: Buses and minibuses conveying persons for reward have a speed limit of 100 km/h.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Speed Limit for a Particular Class of Vehicles
question: Which specific heavy and breakdown vehicles are subject to an 80 km/h speed limit?
body: An 80 km/h speed limit applies to: (i) a goods vehicle with a GVM over 9000kg, (ii) a combination where the combined GVM of the goods vehicle and trailer(s) exceeds 9000kg, (iii) an articulated vehicle whose truck-tractor GCM exceeds 9000kg, and (iv) any breakdown vehicle towing another vehicle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are the maximum permitted overall lengths for different types of motor vehicles and combinations?
body: Maximum vehicle lengths: (i) 8 metres for a trailer (not semi-trailer) under 12,000kg GVM; (ii) 12.5 metres for one over 12,000kg GVM; (iii) 18.5 metres for an articulated motor vehicle; (iv) 22 metres for a bus-train or any combination of motor vehicles; (v) 12.5 metres for any other vehicle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is the maximum permitted overall height for motor vehicles?
body: A double-deck bus (with load) may not exceed 4.65 metres in height; any other motor vehicle may not exceed 4.3 metres.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are the maximum permitted overall widths for different classes of motor vehicles?
body: A bus with a front wheel track over 1.9 metres may not exceed 2.6 metres overall width; a goods vehicle of 12,000kg GVM or more may not exceed 2.6 metres; any other vehicle may not exceed 2.5 metres.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must goods be loaded relative to the road surface and the driver's view?
body: Goods may not be loaded so that they touch the road surface, or obstruct the driver's view to the front, either side, or in the rear-view mirror.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must goods be secured on a vehicle to prevent falling or spilling?
body: Goods must be safely contained within, or securely fastened to, the vehicle, and protected from falling or spilling.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What height limit applies to goods loaded on a motor car's roof?
body: On a motor car's roof, goods may not exceed half the car's height measured from ground level, except pedal cycles.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must a shipping container with twist-lock provisions be secured?
body: A shipping container fitted with twist-lock provisions must be secured with at least four twist locks.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Where should baggage be placed on a motorcycle?
body: Baggage on a motorcycle should be placed in carriers securely attached to the motorcycle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Circumstances Under Which Persons May Be Carried on a Goods Vehicle
question: How high must the enclosure be on a goods vehicle carrying passengers?
body: The section of a goods vehicle carrying persons must be enclosed to at least 350mm above a seated person, or 900mm above a standing person.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Circumstances Under Which Persons May Be Carried on a Goods Vehicle
question: Are passengers permitted to ride inside a caravan while it is being towed?
body: It is against the law for passengers to ride in a caravan.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are the maximum projection limits for a load carried on a motorcycle or sidecar?
body: A motorcycle's load (or sidecar load) may not project more than: (i) 600mm in front of the front axle, (ii) 900mm behind the rear axle, (iii) 450mm to either side, or (iv) 300mm beyond the sidecar wheel.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are the maximum sideways projection limits for goods on a light or heavy vehicle?
body: A light or heavy vehicle's goods may not project sideways from the centre-line by more than 1.3 metres (bus or goods vehicle over 12,000kg GVM) or 1.25 metres (any other vehicle), excluding mirrors or indicators.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How far may goods project beyond the front and rear of a light or heavy vehicle?
body: A light or heavy vehicle's goods may not project more than 300mm beyond the front of the vehicle, or 1.8 metres beyond the rear.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How far may a bracket project beyond the widest part of a vehicle?
body: A light or heavy vehicle may not have a bracket projecting more than 150mm beyond the vehicle's widest part (side mirrors and indicators excepted).

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must a projecting load be marked during the day and at night?
body: A load projecting more than 150mm to the side, or 300mm to the rear, must be marked with a red flag (300mm x 300mm) during the day, and white (front) or red (rear) retro-reflectors at night or whenever visibility is poor.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: On which roadway must a driver travel on a divided public road?
body: On a public road divided into two or more roadways, drive only on the left-hand roadway, unless directed or permitted otherwise by a road traffic sign or a traffic officer.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Driving on Left Side of Roadway
question: On which side of the roadway must a vehicle normally be driven?
body: Drive on the left side of the roadway, without encroaching right, unless it can be done safely or you're directed otherwise by a sign or traffic officer.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Driving on Left Side of Roadway
question: How must a driver react when being passed by another vehicle?
body: When another vehicle wants to pass you, keep as near to the left edge of the roadway as is safely possible, and don't speed up until it has passed.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Driving on Left Side of Roadway
question: What restriction applies when passing oncoming traffic on a roadway?
body: When passing oncoming traffic, don't encroach onto the roadway to your right in a way that obstructs or endangers it.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Driving on Left Side of Roadway
question: What duty applies to a driver passing a stationary bus?
body: A driver passing a stationary bus must do so with due care for people approaching or leaving it.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Prohibition on Driving on Shoulder of Road
question: Under what conditions may a light motor vehicle drive on the shoulder of a public road?
body: A light motor vehicle may not drive on the shoulder of a public road, except: (i) between sunrise and sunset, (ii) while being overtaken on a single-lane-each-way road, (iii) if it can be done safely, and (iv) if visibility is at least 150 metres.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When is changing lanes permitted on a road divided into lanes?
body: On a road divided into lanes by markings, don't change lanes unless it can be done without obstructing or endangering other traffic.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What requirement applies before a driver stops or turns a vehicle?
body: Before stopping or turning, give a clear, timely signal of your intention, long enough and visible enough to warn anyone approaching from the front, rear, or side.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What direction indicators must a motor vehicle be equipped with?
body: A motor vehicle must be equipped with flasher-type direction indicators on both sides.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When must direction indicators be used while driving?
body: Direction indicators must be used every time you turn left or right, or change lanes.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What color and visibility standards apply to a light motor vehicle's direction indicators?
body: A light motor vehicle's indicators must: (i) flash intermittently, (ii) be clearly visible at 30 metres in daylight, and (iii) show white, yellow, or amber light to the front, and yellow, amber, or red light to the rear.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What rear retro-reflector requirement applies to a motorcycle, sidecar, or motor tricycle?
body: A motorcycle, motorcycle with sidecar, or motor tricycle must have a red retro-reflector fitted at the rear.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What retro-reflector requirements apply to the rear of a light motor vehicle?
body: A light motor vehicle must have two red retro-reflectors at the rear, one on each side.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What retro-reflector requirements apply to the rear of a heavy motor vehicle?
body: A heavy motor vehicle must have two red retro-reflectors at the same height at the rear, one on each side.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What side retro-reflector requirements apply to long heavy vehicles or combinations?
body: A heavy vehicle or combination longer than 7 metres must have yellow retro-reflectors along each side, spaced so no two successive ones are more than 3.6 metres apart, unless yellow reflective strips are fitted instead.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Which goods vehicles are required to be fitted with yellow reflective material on their sides and rear?
body: Since 1 January 2001, a goods vehicle with a GVM over 10,000kg must have yellow reflective material on its sides and rear; it's optional (but permitted) for vehicles under 10,000kg GVM.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: On which side must a vehicle pass another?
body: Pass another vehicle on the right at a safe distance, and don't return to the left side until safely clear of the vehicle you passed.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Is exceeding the speed limit permitted while overtaking another vehicle?
body: Exceeding the speed limit while overtaking or passing is not permitted.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Under what circumstances is passing another vehicle on the left allowed?
body: Passing on the left is allowed, if it can be done safely, when the vehicle ahead is turning right or has signalled to; on a one-way urban road wide enough for two or more lanes; on an urban road wide enough for two or more lanes each way; where signs designate lanes on a one-way road; or under a traffic officer's direction.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a driver pass other traffic by driving on the shoulder or verge of a public road?
body: Passing may never be done by driving on the shoulder or the verge of a public road.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When is passing other traffic prohibited on a rise, curve, or restricted visibility area?
body: Don't pass other traffic when approaching the summit of a rise, a curve, or anywhere visibility is too restricted to see oncoming traffic, unless you can do so without encroaching right, or the road is restricted to one direction.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must a driver react when another vehicle wants to pass them?
body: When another vehicle wants to pass you, keep left and don't accelerate until it has passed.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How may a driver signal their intention to overtake a vehicle ahead?
body: A driver wanting to overtake a vehicle ahead (not in the left lane) may signal their intention by flashing their headlights.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is the rule regarding lane positioning and overtaking on a freeway?
body: On a freeway, keep left and overtake on the right.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Who has the right of way at a junction where vehicles move around a traffic island?
body: At a junction where vehicles must move around a traffic island, give way to all traffic approaching from your right, unless a traffic officer or road sign directs you otherwise.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Where is parking prohibited regarding road signs, sidewalks, and entrances?
body: Don't park: (i) where a traffic officer directs otherwise, (ii) in contravention of a sign, (iii) where stopping isn't permitted, (iv) where the vehicle would obscure a road sign, (v) on the sidewalk, or (vi) blocking a private or public vehicular entrance.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How close to a fire hydrant is parking prohibited?
body: Don't park within 1.5 metres of a fire hydrant.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are the restrictions on parking outside an urban area?
body: Outside an urban area, don't park on the roadway (excluding the shoulder), or with any part of the vehicle within 1 metre of the roadway edge, except for reasons beyond your control.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What distance and location restrictions apply to parking within an urban area?
body: Within an urban area, don't park: (i) within 9 metres of the approach side of a pedestrian crossing, (ii) within 5 metres of an intersection, (iii) over a traffic signal's mechanism, (iv) more than 450mm from the kerb, (v) on a road narrower than 5.5 metres, or (vi) on a traffic island, pedestrian mall, or pedestrian lane.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Under what circumstances is stopping on the roadway permitted?
body: Don't stop on the roadway except: (i) to avoid an accident, (ii) on a traffic officer's direction, or (iii) for reasons beyond your control.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Where is stopping prohibited due to potential traffic obstruction or hazard?
body: Don't stop: (i) alongside or opposite an excavation or obstruction if it would obstruct or endanger traffic, (ii) in a tunnel, subway, or on a bridge (or within 6 metres of one), (iii) where the roadway has been narrowed (or within 6 metres of the narrowing), (iv) in contravention of a sign, (v) facing oncoming traffic on the right side, (vi) alongside another vehicle on a road under 9 metres wide, (vii) within a railway level crossing, (viii) within 9 metres of a pedestrian crossing's approach side, or (ix) anywhere it would endanger or obstruct traffic.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is a driver's general duty regarding road traffic signs and rules of the road?
body: Obey every road traffic sign and rule of the road, unless a traffic officer instructs you otherwise.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When is reversing a vehicle permitted?
body: Don't reverse a vehicle unless it can be done safely.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are the minimum required following distances for different types of vehicles?
body: Keep a following distance of at least 2 seconds for light motor vehicles and motorcycles, and at least 3 seconds for heavy motor vehicles; increase this in rain, on a slippery surface, in poor visibility, or when being followed too closely.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What restrictions apply to persons, animals, or objects occupying space inside a vehicle while driving?
body: Don't allow a person, animal, or object to occupy a position that prevents full control of the vehicle, or let anyone interfere with the steering while driving.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What control and view must a driver maintain while driving a vehicle?
body: While driving, maintain complete control of the vehicle and a full view of the road and traffic ahead.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What requirement applies to a vehicle left unattended?
body: An unattended vehicle must have its brake set, or otherwise be secured, so it cannot move from where it was left.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What must a driver do before pulling away from a stationary roadside position?
body: Before pulling away from a parked or stationary roadside position, make sure it's safe and won't interfere with approaching traffic.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must a driver respond to a vehicle sounding a warning device or bell?
body: Always give an immediate, absolute right of way to a vehicle sounding a warning device or bell.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When may a driver let a part of their body protrude from a moving vehicle?
body: Don't let any part of your body protrude from a moving vehicle, except to give a hand signal.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a person or animal occupy an external part of a moving vehicle?
body: Don't allow a person or animal to occupy the roof, a step, a running board, or any other external part of a moving vehicle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What prohibitions apply regarding engine emissions, idling while unattended, and refueling?
body: Don't let the engine: (i) emit abnormal smoke or fumes, (ii) run while the vehicle is stationary and unattended, or (iii) run while fuel is being delivered into the tank.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Is depositing fuel, oil, grease, or flammable matter on a road permitted?
body: Don't deposit fuel, oil, grease, or other flammable or offensive matter on or alongside a road.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a vehicle be driven, pulled, or pushed on a sidewalk?
body: Don't drive, pull, or push a vehicle on a sidewalk.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is a motorcycle rider's general duty regarding road signs and rules?
body: A motorcycle rider must obey every road sign and rule of the road, unless a traffic officer instructs otherwise.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What position must a motorcycle rider maintain while riding?
body: A rider's feet must rest on the front foot rests, seated astride the saddle, with at least one hand on the handlebars at all times.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What requirements apply to carrying a passenger on a motorcycle?
body: A passenger must be briefed by the rider, seated on a securely fastened seat, with feet on securely fastened foot rests, astride the motorcycle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How many people may ride on a motorcycle, excluding a sidecar?
body: No more than two people may ride on a motorcycle, excluding anyone in an attached sidecar.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What engine capacity and seating requirements apply to carrying a passenger on a motorcycle?
body: A passenger may only be carried if the motorcycle's engine exceeds 50cc, and the passenger must be seated in a sidecar or astride a pillion.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How many adults may be carried in a motorcycle sidecar?
body: No more than two adults may be carried in a sidecar attached to a motorcycle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What restrictions apply to carrying objects or persons in front of a motorcycle rider?
body: A rider may not carry a person, animal, or bulky object in front of them; a non-bulky object may be carried if securely attached and doesn't obstruct the rider's view or control.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a motorcycle rider or passenger hold onto another moving vehicle?
body: Neither the rider nor passenger may take hold of another vehicle that is in motion.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What rule applies to a motorcycle's wheels while riding?
body: All wheels of the motorcycle must stay in contact with the road surface at all times.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What formation and overtaking rules apply to motorcycle riders sharing a lane?
body: Riders must travel in single file within the same lane, except briefly to overtake another motorcycle; two motorcycles may not overtake another vehicle at the same time.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Manner in Which a Side Car Is to Be Attached to a Motorcycle
question: On which side must a sidecar be attached?
body: A sidecar must be attached to the left side of the motorcycle, and may not be fitted to a motorcycle with an engine under 50cc.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What restriction applies to holding a cellular device while driving?
body: A driver may not hold a cellular or other communication device in one or both hands, or with any other part of the body, while driving.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What duty does a driver owe to a pedestrian within a pedestrian crossing?
body: A driver must yield right of way, slow down, or stop for a pedestrian crossing a roadway within a pedestrian crossing.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a driver pass a vehicle that has stopped at a pedestrian crossing?
body: A driver may not pass a vehicle that has stopped at a pedestrian crossing.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must pedestrians obey red figure light signals at pedestrian crossings?
body: Pedestrians: (i) may not cross while the red man light is showing; (ii) if the red man flashes, pedestrians already in the road must finish crossing quickly, while those not yet in the road must wait for the green man.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When is a stationary vehicle deemed to be abandoned by its owner?
body: A vehicle left in the same place for more than 24 hours (outside an urban area) or 7 days (within an urban area) is deemed abandoned by its owner.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What actions involving vehicle wheels or movement that cause road damage are prohibited?
body: Don't: (i) cause a vehicle's wheel to drag or spin on the roadway (except in an emergency), (ii) use chocks or shoes between a moving wheel and the road surface, or (iii) otherwise use or move a vehicle in a way that damages the road.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Which specific vehicle types are prohibited from using a freeway?
body: Animal-drawn vehicles, pedal cycles, motorcycles under 50cc or electrically propelled, motor quadrucycles, disability vehicles under 230kg, and tractors (outside road construction or maintenance use) may not use a freeway.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Under what circumstances is stopping on a freeway permitted?
body: Don't stop on a freeway except: (i) by sign or traffic officer direction, (ii) in a designated stopping/parking area, or (iii) for reasons beyond your control.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What actions regarding hand signals, pedestrians, and animals are prohibited on a freeway?
body: (i) Don't give a hand signal on a freeway (except for reasons beyond your control), (ii) be on a freeway on foot, or (iii) leave an animal where it could stray onto one.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What duty applies when a vehicle ahead wants to merge from a freeway on-ramp?
body: If a vehicle ahead wants to merge from an on-ramp, you must allow it to merge in front of you.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a motorcycle be used to tow another vehicle?
body: A motorcycle may not be used to tow another vehicle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is the maximum permitted length for a tow-rope, chain, or tow-bar?
body: The tow-rope, chain, or tow-bar between two vehicles may not exceed 3.5 metres in length.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When is a draw-bar or tow-bar connection required instead of a rope or chain for towing?
body: Towing at over 30 km/h with a rope or chain is not allowed -- a draw-bar or tow-bar connection is required instead.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When may a towed vehicle carry passengers at speeds over 30 km/h?
body: A towed vehicle may only carry passengers at over 30 km/h if it is a semi-trailer.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Who is required to control the steering of a towed vehicle?
body: The towed vehicle's steering must be controlled by a person licensed to drive that class of vehicle.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: How must a towed vehicle be connected if its brakes do not comply with requirements?
body: If the towed vehicle's brakes don't comply with requirements, it must be connected by a draw-bar or tow-bar rather than a rope or chain.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Restriction on Combination of Motor Vehicles
question: What is the maximum number of trailers or other motor vehicles a drawing vehicle may tow?
body: A drawing vehicle may tow a maximum of: (i) two trailers, or (ii) one other motor vehicle that isn't a trailer.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Restriction on Combination of Motor Vehicles
question: What vehicle towing combination is permitted in an emergency?
body: In an emergency, it is permitted to tow one other motor vehicle (not a trailer) together with a trailer.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What condition must be met before crossing or entering a public road?
body: Don't cross or enter a public road unless it's clear of moving traffic for a sufficient distance, or you can do so with safety to yourself and other traffic.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Under what circumstances is a driver required to make a compulsory stop?
body: Stop: (i) as directed by a road traffic sign or a uniformed traffic officer, (ii) at the request or signal of a person leading livestock (cattle, horse, donkey, mule, sheep, goat, pig, or ostrich), or (iii) when animals are crossing the road -- only proceeding once all have crossed and it's safe.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is the minimum required tyre tread depth for a light motor vehicle?
body: A light motor vehicle's tyres must show a clearly visible tread pattern across the full breadth and circumference, at least 1mm deep.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What tyre tread depth requirement applies to a motorcycle with an engine capacity over 50cc?
body: A motorcycle with an engine over 50cc must have tyres showing a clearly visible tread pattern across the full breadth and circumference, at least 1mm deep.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What minimum tread pattern requirement applies to tyres on a motorcycle with an engine of 50cc or under?
body: A motorcycle with an engine of 50cc or under may not run a tyre with less than 80% visible tread pattern across the tread width.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: May a motorcycle be fitted with a retreaded tyre?
body: A motorcycle may not be fitted with a retreaded tyre.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are a driver's immediate duties after being involved in or contributing to an accident?
body: After being involved in or contributing to an accident, a driver must: (i) stop immediately, (ii) check for and assist with any injuries, and (iii) assess the damage.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What information must a driver provide at an accident scene if requested on reasonable grounds?
body: If asked by someone with reasonable grounds, a driver must give: (i) their name and address, (ii) the vehicle owner's name and address, and (iii) the vehicle's registration number.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Within what time frame must an accident be reported to a police station if details were not given at the scene?
body: If these details haven't already been given to a traffic officer at the scene, the accident must be reported to a police station within 24 hours, along with any further information required.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What restriction applies to consuming alcohol or narcotic drugs after an accident before reporting it?
body: Except on a medical practitioner's instruction, a driver may not consume alcohol or narcotic drugs before reporting an accident.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: When an accident causes injury or death and fully obstructs the road, when may a vehicle be moved?
body: If a person has been killed or injured and the accident fully obstructs the roadway, a vehicle may not be moved unless: (i) its position is clearly marked on the road, or (ii) a traffic officer authorises its removal.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: Whose permission is required to remove a damaged vehicle from an accident scene?
body: A vehicle damaged in a collision may not be removed from the accident scene without the driver's or owner's permission.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What is the rule regarding inconsiderate driving on a public road?
body: Don't drive on a public road without reasonable consideration for other road users.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What constitutes reckless or negligent driving on a public road?
body: Don't drive recklessly or negligently, or in a manner that wilfully disregards the safety of people or property.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What are the legal blood alcohol concentration limits for ordinary and professional drivers?
body: Don't drive with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05g per 100ml or more (0.02g per 100ml or more for a professional driver).

heading: Road Traffic Rules
question: What prohibition applies regarding driving or occupying the driver's seat while under the influence of alcohol or drugs?
body: Don't drive, or occupy the driver's seat with the engine running, while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a narcotic drug.

heading: Road Traffic Rules
subheading: Fuel Tank, Electrical Wiring and Battery
question: When is a heavy motor vehicle prohibited from being used due to fuel or electrical system defects?
body: A heavy motor vehicle may not be used if its fuel tank, carburettor, or fuel pipes are defective or exposed as a danger, if the fuel tank lacks an effective cap, or if the electrical wiring and battery aren't properly installed, insulated, and maintained.

heading: Definitions
question: What forms of documentation constitute acceptable identification?
body: Acceptable identification includes: (i) a South African ID document or card, (ii) a valid South African passport, (iii) a foreign ID or traffic register number certificate (for non-residents), or (iv) a driving licence card.

heading: Definitions
question: How is an articulated motor vehicle defined?
body: An articulated motor vehicle is a combination of a truck-tractor and a semi-trailer.

heading: Definitions
question: What structures are included in the definition of a bridge?
body: A bridge includes a culvert and a causeway.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a bus defined regarding passenger capacity?
body: A bus is a motor vehicle designed or adapted to carry more than 16 people, including the driver.

heading: Definitions
question: What constitutes a combination of motor vehicles?
body: A combination of motor vehicles means two or more motor vehicles coupled together.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the definition of a dedicated lane?
body: A dedicated lane is a portion of road reserved for certain periods for the exclusive use of certain vehicle categories, as shown by an appropriate sign.

heading: Definitions
question: What is a direction indicator?
body: A direction indicator is a device fitted to a vehicle allowing the driver to signal an intention to change direction left or right.

heading: Definitions
question: What does the abbreviation DLTC stand for?
body: DLTC stands for Driving Licence Testing Centre, registered under the National Road Traffic Act.

heading: Definitions
question: Who is classified as a driver under the traffic regulations?
body: A driver is any person who: (i) drives or attempts to drive a vehicle, (ii) rides or attempts to ride a pedal cycle, or (iii) leads a draught, pack, or saddle animal, or a herd or flock of animals.

heading: Definitions
question: How is the edge of the roadway defined?
body: The edge of the roadway is the boundary between the roadway and the shoulder, as indicated by a sign, or otherwise the edge of the surfaced or improved part of the road.

heading: Definitions
question: What defines a public road as a freeway?
body: A freeway is a public road, or section of one, designated as a freeway by an appropriate road traffic sign.

heading: Definitions
question: How is the term goods defined in road traffic law?
body: Goods means any movable property.

heading: Definitions
question: What constitutes a goods vehicle?
body: A goods vehicle is a motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle, tricycle, quadrucycle, motor car, minibus, or bus) designed to carry goods on a public road; it includes a truck-tractor, adaptor dolly, converter dolly, and breakdown vehicle.

heading: Definitions
question: How is Gross Combination Mass (GCM) defined?
body: Gross Combination Mass (GCM) is the maximum mass of a vehicle combination (including the drawing vehicle) and its load, as specified by the manufacturer or, failing that, the registering authority.

heading: Definitions
question: How is Gross Vehicle Mass (GVM) defined?
body: Gross Vehicle Mass (GVM) is the maximum mass of a vehicle and its load, as specified by the manufacturer or, failing that, the registering authority.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a haulage tractor defined?
body: A haulage tractor is a motor vehicle designed mainly for drawing other vehicles, with a GCM exceeding 24,000kg; it does not include a truck-tractor or tractor.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the definition of an intersection?
body: An intersection is the area where two or more public roads open to vehicular traffic join or cross at any angle.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a junction defined within an intersection?
body: A junction is the portion of an intersection within the lateral limits of the intersecting roadways, including any stop or yield line marking painted there.

heading: Definitions
question: What is a licence disc?
body: A licence disc is a disc issued under the Act that licenses a vehicle for use on a public road, valid for 12 months.

heading: Definitions
question: What passenger carrying capacity defines a midibus?
body: A midibus is a sub-category of bus designed to carry more than 16 and up to 35 people, including the driver.

heading: Definitions
question: What passenger carrying capacity defines a minibus?
body: A minibus is a motor vehicle designed to carry more than nine but not more than 16 people, including the driver.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a motor car defined regarding passenger capacity?
body: A motor car is a motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle, tricycle, or quadrucycle) designed to carry not more than nine people, including the driver.

heading: Definitions
question: What defines a motorcycle?
body: A motorcycle is a motor vehicle with two wheels, including one with a sidecar attached.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a motor quadrucycle defined?
body: A motor quadrucycle is a motor vehicle (other than a tractor) with four wheels, designed to be driven using motorcycle-type controls.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a motor tricycle defined?
body: A motor tricycle is a motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle or tractor) with three wheels, designed to be driven using motorcycle-type controls.

heading: Definitions
question: What vehicles are included in the definition of a motor vehicle?
body: A motor vehicle is any self-propelled vehicle, including a trailer and a pedal-and-motor vehicle designed to be propelled by pedals, an engine, or both.

heading: Definitions
question: What is a number plate?
body: A number plate is a prescribed plate displaying a vehicle's licence number or a motor trade number.

heading: Definitions
question: What area constitutes a pedestrian crossing?
body: A pedestrian crossing is a portion of road designated as such by a sign, or, absent a sign, the portion at an intersection within the extension of the kerb line and adjacent boundary line.

heading: Definitions
question: What requirement must a professional driver meet to operate a prescribed motor vehicle?
body: A professional driver drives a motor vehicle of a prescribed class and must hold a professional driving permit; this doesn't apply to a learner accompanied by a registered professional driver for that class.

heading: Definitions
question: What is included in the definition of a public road?
body: A public road is any road, street, or thoroughfare commonly used by, or open to, the public, including its verge and any bridge, ferry, or drift it crosses.

heading: Definitions
question: What specification must a retro-reflector comply with?
body: A retro-reflector is a reflector complying with SABS specification 513, bearing a certification or approval mark.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the purpose of a road traffic sign?
body: A road traffic sign is a sign for prohibiting, limiting, regulating, or controlling traffic (in general or a particular class) on a public road.

heading: Definitions
question: What is defined as the roadway?
body: The roadway is the portion of a road built or intended for vehicular traffic, between the edges of the roadway.

heading: Definitions
question: What design feature defines a semi-trailer regarding its tare distribution?
body: A semi-trailer is a trailer with no front axle, designed so at least 15% of its tare is borne by the vehicle drawing it.

heading: Definitions
question: What part of the road is defined as the shoulder?
body: The shoulder is the portion of road between the edge of the roadway and the kerb line.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a vehicle's tare mass calculated?
body: Tare, for a vehicle, is its mass ready to travel on a road, including standard accessories and permanent structural parts, but excluding fuel.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the function of a traffic island?
body: A traffic island is a physical island that channels traffic within a junction or on a public road.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a traffic lane defined?
body: A traffic lane is a longitudinal division of a road wide enough for a single line of vehicles.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the definition and function of a traffic signal?
body: A traffic signal is a road traffic sign that, by automatic light signals, alternately directs traffic to stop and permits it to proceed.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a tractor defined regarding drawing capacity and weight limits?
body: A tractor is a motor vehicle designed mainly for drawing other vehicles with a GCM not exceeding 24,000kg; it does not include a truck-tractor.

heading: Definitions
question: What defines a trailer?
body: A trailer is a vehicle not self-propelled, designed to be drawn by a motor vehicle, excluding a motorcycle sidecar.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a truck-tractor defined?
body: A truck-tractor is a motor vehicle designed for drawing other vehicles, carrying no load other than that of a semi-trailer or ballast; it does not include a tractor or haulage tractor.

heading: Definitions
question: What area is defined as an urban area?
body: An urban area is a local authority area that has been surveyed and subdivided into erven, including the public roads bordering it.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a vehicle defined under road traffic regulations?
body: A vehicle is a device designed mainly to travel on wheels or crawler tracks (excluding devices that move solely on rails).

heading: Definitions
question: What portion of a road is defined as the verge?
body: A verge is the portion of a road, including the sidewalk, that is not the roadway or the shoulder.

heading: Definitions
question: What weight limits define a Light Motor Vehicle (LMV)?
body: LMV means Light Motor Vehicle -- tare/GVM not exceeding 3500kg.

heading: Definitions
question: What specifications define a Heavy Motor Vehicle (HMV)?
body: HMV means Heavy Motor Vehicle -- tare exceeds 3500kg, or a minibus/bus/goods vehicle GVM exceeds 3500kg, or an articulated/combination vehicle's GCM (or trailer GVM) exceeds the prescribed thresholds.

heading: Definitions
question: What vehicle types are included under the motorcycle classification?
body: MC means Motorcycle, and includes a motorcycle, tricycle, and quadrucycle.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: What requirement applies to driving a vehicle on a public road regarding driver licensing?
body: No person may drive a motor vehicle on a public road except under a licence issued in terms of the National Road Traffic Act, and must keep that licence (or document) with them in the vehicle.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: What types of driving licences are issued by testing centres?
body: A licence to drive a motor vehicle is issued by a driving licence testing centre, and is either a provisional licence (a learner's licence) or a full driving licence.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: What documents and fees are required when applying for a learner's licence?
body: A learner's licence application is made at a DLTC on form LL1, accompanied by: (i) two identical photos, (ii) acceptable identification (plus a copy), and (iii) the appropriate fee; applicants 65 or older must also submit a medical certificate (form MC) from a medical practitioner or occupational health practitioner.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: Within what time frame must a licence holder report a permanent change of address?
body: A licence holder who permanently changes their place of residence must notify the registering authority of their new residential and postal address within 14 days.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: What duty does a vehicle owner or operator have regarding driver licensing?
body: An owner, operator, or person in charge of a vehicle may not employ or permit anyone to drive it on a public road unless that person is licensed to drive it.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: Who must hold a professional driving permit to operate a vehicle of a prescribed class?
body: A person may not drive a motor vehicle of a prescribed class without a professional driving permit (kept with them in the vehicle), except a learner accompanied by someone registered as a professional driver for that class.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: How long are a motor vehicle licence and licence disc valid?
body: A motor vehicle licence and licence disc are valid for 12 months from the first day of the month of issue; the expiry date is shown on both.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: Who is responsible for offences committed with a vehicle on a public road?
body: The owner of a vehicle is responsible for all offences committed with it on a public road, if the owner permitted its use.

heading: Licensing & Codes
question: How long is the period of grace to operate a vehicle after its licence expires?
body: A motor vehicle may still be operated for up to 21 days after its licence expires (a 'period of grace'), provided the previous licence number and disc are displayed in the prescribed manner.

heading: Definitions
question: What does it mean to cross a public road?
body: To 'cross' a public road means to move in a direction that intersects the normal course of travel of traffic on that road.

heading: Definitions
question: How is drawing distinguished from general towing?
body: 'Drawing' means towing a vehicle that is designed or adapted solely to be drawn, using a vehicle designed or adapted solely for that purpose -- as distinct from general 'towing'.

heading: Definitions
question: What is a driving licence card?
body: A driving licence card is a driving licence card issued in terms of the National Road Traffic Act.

heading: Definitions
question: What constitutes driving time for a driver?
body: 'Driving time' is any period a driver occupies the driver's seat of a vehicle while it is being operated on a public road, or while the engine is running.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the definition of an emergency brake?
body: An emergency brake is a brake, other than the service brake, that is able to stop a vehicle.

heading: Definitions
question: How is the front end of a vehicle defined?
body: The 'front end' of a vehicle is the part that projects furthest forward (for a semi-trailer, a line through the kingpin connecting the vehicle's widest point ahead of it).

heading: Definitions
question: Who is classified as a driving instructor?
body: An instructor is someone who, for direct reward, teaches another person to drive a motor vehicle, or teaches the rules of the road or road signs for a learner's or driving licence.

heading: Definitions
question: How is the kerb line defined?
body: The kerb line is the boundary between the shoulder and the verge, or, where there's no shoulder, the boundary between the edge of the roadway and the verge.

heading: Definitions
question: How is a medical practitioner defined under the Act?
body: A medical practitioner is a person registered as such under the Medical, Dental and Supplementary Health Service Professions Act.

heading: Definitions
question: What does it mean to operate a vehicle on a public road?
body: To 'operate on a public road' means to use or drive a vehicle (or permit it to be used or driven), or to have or permit a vehicle to be on a public road.

heading: Definitions
question: How is the overall length of a vehicle or combination measured?
body: Overall length is the distance between the front end and rear end of a vehicle, or (for a combination) between the front of the leading vehicle and the rear of the rearmost vehicle.

heading: Definitions
question: How is overall height measured for a motor vehicle?
body: Overall height is the distance from ground level to the highest point of the vehicle or its load, excluding overhead electrical contacting gear or a catwalk on electrically driven vehicles.

heading: Definitions
question: How is the overall width of a vehicle determined?
body: Overall width is the distance between two planes parallel to the vehicle's centre-line, touching the widest projecting points on either side -- excluding side mirrors, direction indicators, or small fitments like air deflectors.

heading: Definitions
question: Who is considered the owner of a vehicle?
body: The 'owner' of a vehicle is the person with the right to use and enjoy it under common law or a contractual agreement, or a motor dealer in possession of it for sale.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the legal definition of parking a vehicle?
body: To 'park' means to keep a vehicle stationary for longer than is reasonably necessary to load or unload people or goods, excluding delays beyond the driver's control.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the definition and primary function of a parking brake?
body: A parking brake is a brake, normally a hand brake, used to keep a vehicle stationary.

heading: Definitions
question: What is defined as the rear end of a vehicle?
body: The 'rear end' of a vehicle is the part that projects furthest to the rear.

heading: Definitions
question: What does it mean for a vehicle to be roadworthy?
body: 'Roadworthy', for a vehicle, means it complies with the relevant legal provisions and is otherwise fit to be operated on a public road.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the definition and primary function of a service brake?
body: A service brake is a brake, normally a footbrake, used to reduce a vehicle's speed or bring it to a stop.

heading: Definitions
question: What part of a verge is defined as a sidewalk?
body: A sidewalk is the portion of a verge intended for the exclusive use of pedestrians.

heading: Definitions
question: What is the legal definition of the term stop?
body: To 'stop' means to bring a vehicle to a standstill.

heading: Definitions
question: What legislation does the term The Act refer to in South African road traffic law?
body: 'The Act' refers to the National Road Traffic Act, 1996 (Act No. 93 of 1996), which governs road traffic in South Africa.

heading: Definitions
question: How is towing defined in contrast to drawing?
body: 'Towing' means towing a vehicle that is not designed or adapted solely to be drawn -- as distinct from 'drawing', which refers to vehicles built solely for that purpose.
